variants.headline: Party leader blunders in election debate
variants.sub: An election debate has included a blunder by {leader}, leader of {party}.
variants.body:
The leader of {party}, {leader}, has blundered in an election debate. The misstep is established, but the words involved and their effect on voters are not supplied here. Readers assessing {target} should distinguish the debate event from a fabricated quotation or a claim that the election's outcome has been decided.

A debate error is not an economic programme or an electoral result. Business readers should avoid pricing an imagined policy reversal into a speaking mistake. A sound assessment distinguishes communication, political judgment and actual decisions, rather than treating a blunder as a complete forecast of what a party would do.

We criticise {target} in this assessment. Political leadership includes judgment under scrutiny, and a debate blunder is an appropriate occasion to question whether the standard of public presentation has been adequate. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.
